questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to cook traditional food from different countries around the world
The history of bread
Why street food is becoming so popular in the UK
Why British pubs serve bad food
questions.why: The topic is street food and why it has become so popular in the UK.

questions.q: What does Rob like about street food in London?
options: Food from all over the world is cooked in front of you
It is always much cheaper than eating in a restaurant
It is healthier than home cooking
It is a very old British tradition
questions.why: Rob says you can find delicious foods from all over the world, cooked in front of you.

questions.q: What do Neil and Rob say about street food in Britain?
options: It has always been an important part of British life and culture
It is losing popularity
It is only found in London
It isn't really a British tradition, but it's popular now
questions.why: Neil says it's not really a British tradition and Rob agrees, but says it's much more popular these days.

questions.q: According to Mark Laurie, where is street food growing?
options: Only in London
In big cities and more and more outside them
Mainly in small villages in the countryside
Only at music festivals
questions.why: He says it's growing in the bigger cities and increasingly in the provinces.

questions.q: What does Mark Laurie mean when he says street food has become mainstream?
options: It is only for young people
It is expensive
It is a normal, accepted part of everyday eating
It is sold in supermarkets as well as on the street
questions.why: Rob explains it's no longer seen as unusual; it's becoming an accepted part of everyday eating.

questions.q: Why, according to Mark Laurie, do people like street food?
options: It is honest, real food made by people you trust
It is quick to eat
It is sold late at night when other places are closed
It is cooked in microwaves
questions.why: He says 'It's honest food, it's authentic food and it's people that you can trust making it.'

questions.q: What does Mark Laurie compare street food with?
options: Expensive restaurant meals
Food cooked at home
Fast food from burger chains
Microwave food you might get in a pub
questions.why: He says 'It's not some microwave food... that you might get in your local pub.'

questions.q: What is Neil's attitude to microwave meals?
options: He thinks they are dangerous
He quite likes them now and then
He never eats them
He thinks they are authentic
questions.why: Neil says 'I quite like a microwave meal now and then'.
